clips.text: What is the supreme law of the land?
The U.S. Constitution.
The Constitution sets up the federal government and protects the basic rights of everyone in the country. Every other law must follow it.
How many U.S. senators are there?
One hundred.
Each of the fifty states elects two senators, no matter how many people live there. Two times fifty makes one hundred.
Who vetoes bills?
The President of the United States.
Congress writes and passes bills. The President can sign a bill into law, or reject it with a veto. Congress can still override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both chambers.
What is the highest court in the United States?
The Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court is the top of the judicial branch. It has the final word on what the Constitution means, and it can strike down a law that goes against it.
Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
American Indians, or Native Americans.
American Indian nations lived across North America for thousands of years before European explorers and settlers arrived.
Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
Thomas Jefferson.
Thomas Jefferson wrote the first draft of the Declaration of Independence, adopted on July fourth, seventeen seventy-six. He later became the third President.
What is the capital of the United States?
Washington, D.C.
Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state. The White House, Congress and the Supreme Court are all there.
Why does the flag have thirteen stripes?
Because there were thirteen original colonies. Or: because the stripes represent the original colonies.
The thirteen stripes stand for the thirteen British colonies that declared independence in seventeen seventy-six. The fifty stars stand for today's fifty states.
Who was the first President?
When do people vote?
Who lives in the White House?
Washington was the first President.
Citizens can vote.
The President lives in the White House.
